Pathetic

/puh-THET-ik/ — rhymes with 'athletic' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pathetic is so weak or inadequate that it deserves pity or scorn.

The umbrella offered pathetic protection against the sideways hail.

Worked Example

The school's 'security system' was a rusty gate that no longer latched and a camera that had been broken for years. When bikes went missing from the rack, no one was surprised.

The security was pathetic — miserably inadequate for its job. 'Imperfect' security merely has some gaps; pathetic security fails so completely it invites pity or scorn.

How Pathetic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

pitiful

pitiful: deserving pity for its weakness

feeble

feeble: weak and lacking force

woeful

woeful: deplorably bad

Antonyms

admirable

admirable: deserving respect and approval

impressive

impressive: commanding attention through excellence

How Strong Is It? — mediocre → abysmal → pathetic

mediocre vs. pathetic

mediocre vs. pathetic: Mediocre is weaker than pathetic — mediocre work is merely average and forgettable, while pathetic work fails badly enough to invite scorn.

abysmal vs. pathetic

abysmal vs. pathetic: Abysmal is stronger than pathetic — pathetic means miserably inadequate, but abysmal means bottomlessly, catastrophically bad.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — path-

root — path-: feeling, suffering (Greek)

suffix — -etic

suffix — -etic: relating to (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Greek pathos means 'feeling' or 'suffering.' Pathetic originally meant 'stirring the feelings'; today it names things so inadequate that the feeling they stir is pity.
